d: Animation Capture in the Animation Editor allows you to generate high-quality, realistic animations for faces and bodies.
h:
import BetaAlert from '../includes/beta-features/beta-alert.md'

You can record or upload video content to the Animation Editor to quickly capture movement and expressions as animation keyframes. These tools can create unique and realistic animations within minutes while providing access to the animation keyframes for additional adjustments.

The animation capture tools allow you to:

  • Record your face with a webcam to puppeteer characters with animation compatible heads.
  • Upload full-body video content to generate high quality realistic animations for an entire character.

Face

Animation Capture - Face allows you to use your webcam to puppeteer rigs with animation compatible heads and generate corresponding keyframes to your movement. With the ability to record up to 60‑second animations, you can quickly provide both your playable and nonplayable characters the means to realistically grin, raise their eyebrows, drop their jaw, or any other expression necessary for your game.

Beta: this feature is still being tested by Roblox and may change.

Before you begin to record your face, ensure that you're in a well lit room close enough to your camera so that your face is in the center of your camera's recording frame. This increases your camera's ability to distinguish you from your surroundings so that you can accurately puppeteer your avatar and create high-quality animations.

  1. From the toolbar's Avatar tab, click Clip Editor. The Animation Editor window displays.
  2. In the 3D viewport or Explorer window, select the rig you want your video to animate. Enter a new animation name in the dialog window and click the Create button.
  3. Navigate to the track list and click the Face Capture button. A popup displays asking you to acknowledge that you consent to the collection of your facial movements to enable the feature and camera access.

  1. OPTIONAL If you have multiple cameras, choose which camera you want to use to record.

  2. In the controls widget in the 3D viewport, click the red circle. Your camera begins recording your facial movements.

  1. When you finish your recording, click either the red square or countdown timer. Keyframes that correspond to your facial movement display within the timeline.

  1. OPTIONAL If you'd like to delete the recording and try again, click Re‑Record.

After you finish your recording, you can fine-tune the keyframes, save your animation, then export it to use across all of your games.

Body

The Animation Capture - Body allows you to quickly generate high-quality, realistic full-body animations for your R15 rigs by uploading videos to use to track the body's movement and generate corresponding keyframes. This significantly speeds up the manual process of creating animations, and allows you to personalize your avatars and NPCs with life-like mannerisms in a few minutes.

Beta: this feature is still being tested by Roblox and may change.

Before you import a video to the Animation Editor, ensure the .mp4 or .mov file meets the following requirements:

  • It includes just one person who is well-lit and visible throughout the video.
  • It only contains a continuous single shot that's less than 15 seconds from a stable camera.
  • It adheres to Roblox's Community Rules and Terms of Use.

To import a video to create an animation:

  1. From the toolbar's Avatar tab, click Clip Editor. The Animation Editor window displays.
  2. In the 3D viewport or the Explorer window hierarchy, select the R15 rig you want your video to animate. Enter a new animation name in the dialog window and click the Create button.
  3. Navigate to the media and playback controls and click the ⋯ button, then navigate to Import ⟩ Live Animation Creator.

  1. In the popup dialog, click the Choose Video button.
  2. Select the video you want to import from your local machine, then click the Open button. After about a minute, keyframes that correspond to movement in your video display within the timeline.

After your import is successful, you can save and export your animation to use across all of your games.

kid.simple: Animation capture lets you make animations by acting them out instead of posing every frame by hand. With Face capture, your webcam copies your facial expressions onto a character with an animation-ready head. With Body capture, you upload a short video of a person moving and Roblox turns it into a full-body animation for an R15 rig. Both create real keyframes you can tweak afterward, save, and publish.
kid.analogy: It is like a motion-capture studio for movies, where an actor's real movements are copied onto a digital character, except you only need a webcam or a phone video.
keyPoints: Both tools are beta features, so you must turn them on in Studio's beta features first.

Face capture: open the Clip Editor from the Avatar tab, select a rig with an animation-compatible head, name the animation, click Face Capture, accept the consent popup, then press the red circle to record.
Face recordings can be up to 60 seconds. Stop with the red square or timer, and click Re-Record to try again.
For good face capture, use a well-lit room and keep your face in the center of the camera view.
Body capture: select an R15 rig, click the three-dot button, then Import, then Live Animation Creator, and choose an `.mp4` or `.mov` video.
Body videos need one well-lit person visible the whole time, one continuous shot under 15 seconds, a steady camera, and must follow Roblox's Community Rules and Terms of Use.
After capture, you can fine-tune keyframes, save, and export the animation like any other.

terms.animation capture: Making an animation by recording real movement instead of posing by hand.
terms.puppeteer: To control a character's movements with your own, like a puppet copying you.
terms.animation compatible head: A character head built to move its face, so it can smile, blink, or drop its jaw.
terms.keyframe: A saved pose at a moment in time. Capture makes these for you automatically.
terms.R15 rig: Roblox's standard 15-part character body, with joints for arms, legs, and torso.
terms.beta feature: A new feature still being tested. You turn it on yourself in Studio's beta features settings.
terms.consent: Saying yes on purpose. The Face Capture popup asks if you agree to your face movements being collected and your camera being used.
terms.NPC: Non-player character, a character controlled by the game instead of a person.

watchOut: Not enabling the beta feature first. The capture buttons will not be available.
Recording in a dark room or off-center. The camera has trouble tracking you; get good light and center your face.
Uploading a video with more than one person, camera cuts, shaky camera, or longer than 15 seconds. Keep it to one person, one steady shot, under 15 seconds.
Using face capture on a rig without an animation-compatible head. Pick a rig with a dynamic head.
